{"parentUuid":"6743f9f6-9755-466e-9a96-86e2ab4f4481","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"53fa6da9-8f7a-4671-b98f-abfb45172e2f","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01CRoKrsAamn6DzbPgewZxCX","type":"tool_result","content":"1\ttitle:\tSpec: Document-style authoring — Editor, tables, Charts, Site preview\n2\tstate:\tOPEN\n3\tauthor:\tDavelleAT (Davelle Ampofo-Twumasi)\n4\tlabels:\tspec\n5\tcomments:\t0\n6\tassignees:\t\n7\tprojects:\t\n8\tmilestone:\t\n9\tissue-type:\t\n10\tparent:\t\n11\tsub-issues:\t\n12\tsub-issues-completed:\t\n13\tblocked-by:\t\n14\tblocking:\t\n15\tnumber:\t14\n16\t--\n17\t## Problem Statement\n18\t\n19\tThe office's writers are IR staff and interns, not web developers, but every Data Bite and Report body is typed as Markdown in a plain textarea. A table means lining up pipes by hand, a chart means making it in Excel, exporting a PNG, uploading it, and typing `image:<name>`, and a link to the Factbook means pasting a URL that breaks if the site moves. The preview under the textarea uses the admin console's styling, so nobody sees the page as a visitor will until after `cms publish`.\n20\t\n21\tGoal: turn the CMS from a Markdown publishing tool into a document-style authoring environment. Nontechnical staff can write, paste, build tables and charts, and preview the exact public result without ever seeing the underlying content format.\n22\t\n23\t## Solution\n24\t\n25\t- The **Editor**, a hand-built visual editor, replaces the Markdown textarea. It has a toolbar, cleans up pasted text, and turns a range pasted from Excel or Sheets into a table. The body is still **stored as Markdown**, so the sanitizer, `cms publish`, and existing content are unchanged (ADR-005).\n26\t- Tables are built and edited in place.\n27\t- A **Chart** is built from data typed or pasted into the CMS and drawn by the server as inline SVG, with its data available as a table (ADR-006, which reverses ADR-004's deferral). Uploaded **Chart images** stay and get an \"Insert image\" button.\n28\t- Links to other Reports and Data Bites are picked from a list and stored by immutable reference, so they stay correct when slugs or the site's address change.\n29\t- A **Site preview** shows the draft as the public page (site nav, stylesheet, date line) beside the Editor and in a new tab, with a \"Draft preview, not published\" banner.\n30\t\n31\tControls are functional and minimally styled. A visual design pass for the admin console comes later, in its own spec.\n32\t\n33\t## User Stories\n34\t\n35\t1. As an Analyst, I want to write a Data Bite with toolbar buttons for bold, italic, lists, headings, and quotes, so that I never have to learn Markdown.\n36\t2. As an Analyst, I want to paste text from Word or Google Docs and keep its bold, lists, headings, and links but not its fonts or colours, so that pasted content matches the site.\n37\t3. As an Analyst, I want to paste a range from Excel or Sheets and get a table, so that I don't retype numbers.\n38\t4. As an Analyst, I want to edit a table in place and add or remove rows and columns, so that fixing a number takes one click.\n39\t5. As a visitor, I want numeric table columns right-aligned, so that figures line up and compare easily.\n40\t6. As an Analyst, I want to build a bar or line chart by typing or pasting data, and see it drawn as I go, so that a survey result gets a chart without Excel exports.\n41\t7. As an Analyst, I want a clear message next to a cell the chart can't read, so that I know exactly what to fix.\n42\t8. As an Analyst, I want suppressed values (`*`, `<10`) to be accepted and marked as suppressed, so that a chart respects small-cell privacy rules.\n43\t9. As a visitor using a screen reader, I want each Chart named by its title and its data available as a table, so that I get the numbers without seeing the chart.\n44\t10. As an Analyst, I want to link to another Report or Data Bite by picking it from a list, so that the link survives slug changes and the site moving.\n45\t11. As a visitor, I want a link to an item that isn't published to show as plain text, not a broken link.\n46\t12. As a Director, I want to be told which items link to an item before I delete it, so that I know which pages will lose a link.\n47\t13. As an Analyst, I want to insert an uploaded Chart image with a button that requires a description, so that I can't forget the alt text.\n48\t14. As an Analyst or Director, I want to see the draft exactly as the public page will look, at desktop and phone widths, so that I catch problems before publishing.\n49\t15. As an Analyst or Director, I want a warning before I leave a page with unsaved changes, so that I don't lose work.\n50\t16. As a Director, I want opening and saving an untouched item to leave its stored body byte-for-byte unchanged, so that the Editor never rewrites content nobody edited.\n51\t\n52\t## Implementation Decisions\n53\t\n54\t### Editor and storage (T13, ADR-005)\n55\t\n56\t- **No dependency.** The Editor is `contenteditable` plus a toolbar in vanilla JS with no build step (ADR-002). It supports current Chrome, Safari, and Firefox.\n57\t- **Markdown stays the storage format.** On load, the server renders the body to Editor HTML with the existing pipeline. On save, the Editor posts its HTML, and the server sanitizes it with nh3 and converts it to Markdown with stdlib `html.parser` (a new module, testable with pytest).\n58\t- **Toolbar:** bold, italic, bulleted list, numbered list, link, Section (H2), Subsection (H3), block quote. The title stays the only H1. There's no underline, font, colour, or alignment, because Markdown can't hold them.\n59\t- **Base version:** the edit form carries `item_base`, a SHA-256 hash of the item's stored `title`, `slug`, and `body` as the page loaded them. The form saves all three, so all three are covered. A hash of the body alone would let a stale tab overwrite someone else's newer title or slug. On save, if the stored item's hash no longer matches (someone else saved in between), the whole save is refused with \"This item changed since you opened it. Reload to see the latest version.\" Nothing is merged, and no field is written.\n60\t- **Untouched is byte-for-byte:** the Editor posts `body_dirty=0` until the writer's first change. With `body_dirty=0` and a matching `item_base`, the server keeps the stored body exactly and ignores the posted HTML. The client can only choose \"keep what is stored\", so trusting the flag grants nothing. Opening the Editor never rewrites the body.\n61\t- **An edited body is saved in standard Markdown form:** any body the Editor has changed is rewritten in one standard form.\n62\t- **Locked blocks:** a top-level block the Editor can't represent shows as a read-only block reading \"This part can't be edited here\" (with a Remove button), and its original bytes are kept even when blocks around it are edited. No current content triggers this. The mechanism:\n63\t  - **Detection:** the stored body is parsed with markdown-it. A top-level block is *supported* only if it and everything inside it is in the Editor's set: paragraph, H2, H3, bulleted and numbered list, block quote, table, a valid `chart` fence, and inline bold, italic, line break, links allowed under T14, and `image:<name>` images. Anything else locks the whole top-level block it sits in, e.g. a code block, raw HTML, H1 or H4 and deeper, a horizontal rule, or an inline code span in a paragraph. Its exact source bytes come from the token's line map.\n64\t  - **Before rendering Editor HTML:** each locked block is cut out of the source and replaced by an opaque token (`locked-<n>`, n being its position among the stored body's locked blocks). The remaining Markdown is rendered, and the token becomes the read-only block. The block's **raw Markdown bytes never reach the browser**: not in the Editor's HTML, not in a hidden field, not in an attribute. What the writer sees is that block's **sanitized rendered HTML** from the ordinary pipeline, displayed read-only next to its token.\n65\t  - **On save:** each token in the posted HTML is replaced by the original fragment taken from the **stored database body** (checked by `item_base`), never from anything the client sent. A token that doesn't exist in the stored body, or appears more than once, refuses the save. A missing token means the writer removed that block, which is allowed.\n66\t- **Paste:** only supported formatting survives. An HTML table on the clipboard (from Excel or Sheets) becomes an Editor table. A pasted or dropped picture is refused with a message pointing to \"Insert image\" (T18).\n67\t- **Unsaved changes:** a `beforeunload` warning is shown when the Editor is dirty. There's no autosave, since that would publish half-finished text on a published Data Bite.\n68\t- **Fallback:** the Editor takes over the existing `body` textarea. If the script fails, the textarea still works and posts Markdown as it does today.\n69\t\n70\t### Links (T14)\n71\t\n72\t- **The rule, restated:** every *site-owned* link and asset uses a relative path. Only an *explicit external link* (`<a href>`) may be absolute, and only as `https:` or `mailto:`. The Editor's link dialog refuses anything else (`http:`, `javascript:`, root-absolute `/…`, other schemes) with a message.\n73\t- **The link pipeline enforces it for every body, however it was saved:** at render time, an `<a>` keeps its href only if the href is `https:`, `mailto:`, or a site reference (below) that resolves. Anything else renders as its link text with no `<a>`. This covers the Markdown fallback and any stored content, not only the Editor. Consequence (approved): a relative path typed by hand, e.g. `[CDS](reports/cds.html)`, renders as plain text, because it would break depending on page depth. Site links are made with the picker.\n74\t- **Images follow the same rule:** only `image:<name>` renders an `<img>`. An absolute image URL (e.g. `![Logo](https://…)`) renders nothing (approved). A hot-linked image sits outside the draft gate that ADR-004 exists for. T14 updates `tests/test_t10_chart_images.py`'s \"other image URLs\" test to match.\n75\t- **Stable references, not ids:** SQLite may reuse the highest deleted `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` (noted in `app/data_bites.py` and `app/reports.py`), so the id isn't safe to link by.\n76\t  - Each Data Bite and Report gets an immutable `ref` column: 32 lowercase hex characters from `secrets.token_hex(16)`, set at creation, never edited, never reused. A new ref is checked, in the same transaction as the insert, against **both** tables' live refs and `deleted_refs`. On the (extremely unlikely) collision, a fresh ref is generated and the insert retried, and it fails loudly after 3 attempts.\n77\t  - It's added through `ADDED_COLUMNS`, with existing rows given refs by `init_db`, plus `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` on each table.\n78\t  - A site link is stored as `report:<ref>` or `data-bite:<ref>` and resolved at render time to the page-relative path, like `image:<name>` (ADR-004). Never by title, slug, or id.\n79\t- **Deleted versus never existed:** deleting a Data Bite or Report writes a tombstone row `deleted_refs(kind, ref, deleted_at)` in the same transaction. A ref found in its table is a live or draft item. A ref found only in `deleted_refs` was deleted. A ref in neither never existed (e.g. typed by hand in the fallback).\n80\t- **Unresolvable targets:** a draft, unpublished, deleted, or never-existing target renders as **plain text** (its link text, with no `<a>`), never as an empty or unsafe link. The reference stays stored, so it becomes a link again if its target is published.\n81\t- In the Editor, such links are marked \"Not published: will show as plain text\", \"Item deleted\", or \"Unknown link\".\n82\t- Deleting an item shows the items whose bodies link to it, and the delete isn't blocked.\n83\t- `cms publish` regenerates all of `site/` on every run (`app/publish.py`), so a link becomes live on the first publish after its target is published. No pages need rebuilding individually.\n84\t- **Docs and crawler change together in T14:**\n85\t  - The CLAUDE.md hard rule becomes \"Site-owned links and assets use **relative** paths only. Never `href=\"/...\"` or `src=\"/...\"`. Explicit external links may use `https:` or `mailto:`.\" ADR-001 gets a matching note.\n86\t  - The T07/T08 crawler skips an `<a href>` that is `https:` or `mailto:`. It still fails on any root-absolute path, any other `://` URL, and any `src` that isn't relative, and it still fetches and checks every internal link.\n87\t\n88\t### Tables (T15)\n89\t\n90\t- Edited in place in the Editor, with add/remove row and column controls shown while the cursor is in a table. Stored as a Markdown table (T09 styling and scroll wrapper unchanged).\n91\t- The first row is always the header.\n92\t- **Right-aligned automatically** when every non-empty cell in a column is numeric. Numeric means digits with optional thousands commas, a leading `-` or `$`, a trailing `%`, or accounting parentheses `(3.2)`. Blank, `—`, and `n/a` cells don't stop a column counting as numeric.\n93\t\n94\t### Charts (T16 rendering, ADR-006; T17 builder)\n95\t\n96\t- **Stored** as a fenced block whose info string is exactly `chart`, containing one strict JSON object parsed with stdlib `json`. Writers never see it.\n97\t- **Grammar, version 1:**\n98\t\n99\t  | Key | Required | Type and limits |\n100\t  |---|---|---|\n101\t  | `version` | yes | the integer `1` |\n102\t  | `type` | yes | `\"bar\"`, `\"hbar\"`, or `\"line\"` |\n103\t  | `title` | yes | string, 1 to 120 characters |\n104\t  | `x_label`, `y_label` | no | string, up to 60 characters |\n105\t  | `unit` | no | `{\"text\": string of 1 to 20 characters, \"position\": \"prefix\" or \"suffix\"}` |\n106\t  | `source` | no | string, up to 200 characters |\n107\t  | `categories` | yes | array of 1 to 30 strings for `bar`/`hbar`, or 2 to 60 for `line`; each 1 to 60 characters; no duplicates |\n108\t  | `series` | yes | array of 1 to 4 `{\"name\": string of 1 to 40 characters, \"values\": [...]}`, with names unique and `values` exactly as long as `categories` |\n109\t  | `values[i]` | yes | string, up to 20 characters: the cell **as typed**, parsed at render by the number rules below, so \"as typed\" labels and suppressed notation survive |\n110\t\n111\t  - Every string must be single-line (no control characters, including newlines and tabs) and is Unicode NFC-normalized on save.\n112\t  - Unknown keys, missing required keys, wrong types, duplicate JSON keys (checked with `object_pairs_hook`), `NaN`, `Infinity`, trailing data, and any block over 32 KB make the block **invalid**.\n113\t  - A value cell that fails the number rules is also invalid, unless it's a missing or suppressed value.\n114\t- **Canonical serialization:** keys in the table's order, absent optional keys omitted, `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)`, and a trailing newline inside the fence. The Editor and the fallback both save this form.\n115\t- **Malformed blocks:** validation runs on **every save path**, the Editor and the Markdown fallback alike. A body containing an invalid `chart` block is refused with a form error that names the problem, e.g. \"Chart 2: series 'Fall 2025' has 29 values but 30 categories\". As defense in depth, rendering an invalid block (such as stored content validated under older rules) outputs the fixed text \"This chart could not be shown.\" and nothing else, from no writer-controlled input.\n116\t- **Types:** vertical bar, horizontal bar, line. 1 to 4 series, with a legend when there's more than one. Up to 30 categories for bar charts and 60 for line charts.\n117\t- **Fields:** title (required), x- and y-axis labels (optional), Units (optional; one field in the builder, stored with its prefix or suffix position), Source/note (optional; one line of plain text with no formatting).\n118\t- **Palette:** fixed and accessible, and writers can't choose colours.\n119\t- **Number parsing:** a value may have thousands commas, a leading `-`, accounting parentheses (negative), a trailing `%`, or a leading `$`. Any other currency symbol is an inline error.\n120\t- **Units:** `$` is a unit *prefix* and `%` a unit *suffix*, and the chart stores which one it is. Units typed as a word (\"students\") is a suffix, with a space before it. One chart has one unit, and mixing `$` and `%` is an inline error naming the first conflicting cell. A `%` in the data sets the units to `%` if none are given.\n121\t- **Missing values:** blank, `—`, `n/a`. No bar is drawn, and a line shows a gap.\n122\t- **Suppressed values:** the whole trimmed cell must match `*`, `<N`, `≤N`, or `<=N` (N a whole number).\n123\t  - No mark is drawn.\n124\t  - The data table keeps the original notation.\n125\t  - \"Some values are suppressed for privacy\" appears once under the chart.\n126\t- **Axes:** a bar chart always starts at zero. A line chart may start above zero and says so when it does. Values are labelled as typed, not re-rounded.\n127\t- **Suggested type:** a long category label suggests horizontal bar but doesn't force it.\n128\t- **Accessibility:** the SVG has `role=\"img\"` and the chart title as its accessible name. Under it, a `<details>` \"Show the data\" table is generated from the same data. The public site gets no JavaScript.\n129\t- **Trusted SVG boundary:** nothing inserted after nh3 is sanitized again, so the chart's HTML must be safe because of how it's built, not by filtering.\n130\t  - **Placeholders:** each render generates a fresh `secrets.token_hex(16)` nonce *after* the writer's input is fixed. Each valid chart fence renders as the placeholder `chart-<nonce>-<n>`. After nh3, each placeholder must occur exactly once and is replaced exactly once. A missing, extra, or leftover placeholder fails the render loudly (an exception, and a 500 in the admin console) rather than emitting anything partial.\n131\t  - **Validate first:** a chart is drawn only from a block that passed the full grammar above. Values are parsed to Python `float`s and checked with `math.isfinite`, and anything non-finite is rejected before drawing.\n132\t  - **Fixed vocabulary:** the renderer emits only these elements: `figure`, `figcaption`, `svg`, `g`, `title`, `rect`, `line`, `polyline`, `circle`, `text`, `p`, `small`, `details`, `summary`, `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tr`, `th`, `td`. It emits only these attributes: `class`, `viewBox`, `role`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-hidden`, `id`, `x`, `y`, `x1`, `y1`, `x2`, `y2`, `width`, `height`, `cx`, `cy`, `r`, `points`, `fill`, `stroke`, `stroke-width`, `text-anchor`, `scope`.\n133\t  - **Attribute values:**\n134\t    - Numbers are formatted by the renderer.\n135\t    - `fill` and `stroke` come only from the fixed palette constants.\n136\t    - `class` comes only from fixed class names.\n137\t    - `id` is only `chart-<nonce>-<n>-title`.\n138\t    - There's never an `href`, `style`, `on*`, or URL-bearing attribute.\n139\t  - **Writer text:** every writer-controlled string (title, labels, unit, source, category and series names, cell text) appears only as escaped *text content* (`html.escape`), in both the SVG and the data table. Never as an attribute value, element name, id, class, URL, or CSS.\n140\t  - No uploaded SVG is ever served (ADR-004 unchanged).\n141\t- **Builder (T17):** a dialog with a grid (categories down, series across) that accepts typing and an Excel or Sheets paste. It draws the chart live using the same server rendering, shows errors next to the cells, and has the Units field. In the body, a Chart is a card showing the drawn chart, with Edit and Remove.\n142\t\n143\t### Chart images in the Editor (T18)\n144\t\n145\t- \"Insert image\" lists the item's uploaded Chart images, and a description (alt) is required before inserting. It's stored as `![Description](image:<name>)` as today, and the existing upload, validation, and permissions (ADR-004) are unchanged.\n146\t\n147\t### Site preview (T12)\n148\t\n149\t- The draft is rendered through the public templates, `public_site.CSS`, and the site nav, with the item shown **as if published**: a draft Report appears in the nav. Other drafts stay hidden.\n150\t- It's an embedded frame beside the Editor that drops below it on narrow screens, and it updates as the writer types (debounced, as today).\n151\t- A Desktop/Phone width toggle.\n152\t- \"Preview on site\" opens the same rendering in a new tab, showing the current **unsaved** edits (the form is posted to the tab, and nothing is saved).\n153\t- A \"Draft preview, not published\" banner on every Site preview.\n154\t- Preview routes require login and CSRF, save nothing, and follow the item's permissions (ADR-003).\n155\t\n156\t### Vocabulary\n157\t\n158\t- CONTEXT.md gains **Chart**, **Site preview**, and **Editor**, and **Chart image** is clarified as uploaded.\n159\t- Avoid: graph, WYSIWYG, rich text, live view.\n160\t\n161\t## Testing Decisions\n162\t\n163\t- Behaviour is tested through `TestClient` with the `client` / `client_as(role)` fixtures, as in #1 and #11. The pure modules (HTML → Markdown conversion, chart parsing, SVG drawing) also get direct pytest tests.\n164\t- **Round trip:**\n165\t  - An untouched body posted back is stored byte-for-byte.\n166\t  - A no-change round trip through the standard form renders equivalent HTML, for every seed body and every T09/T10 test fixture.\n167\t  - An edit to one block changes only that block's rendered HTML.\n168\t  - A locked block's bytes survive edits to the blocks around it.\n169\t  - The Editor HTML for a body with locked blocks contains their tokens and their sanitized rendered HTML, and none of their raw Markdown bytes anywhere in the response.\n170\t  - A save with an unknown locked token, a duplicated token, or a forged token that carries its own content is refused. A save with a token removed drops only that block.\n171\t  - A save against a stale `item_base` is refused and changes nothing. **Title/slug conflict:** tab A opens an item, tab B changes only its title (or only its slug) and saves, then tab A saves an untouched body. Tab A's save is refused, and tab B's title and slug survive. A save with `body_dirty=0` stores the old body even when the posted HTML differs.\n172\t- **Sanitizing:** Editor HTML carrying `<script>`, `onerror=`, `style=`, `javascript:` hrefs, root-absolute hrefs, and unknown tags is stored as safe Markdown, with none of it surviving to any render.\n173\t- **Links:**\n174\t  - A `report:<ref>` or `data-bite:<ref>` link renders a correct relative href on the public page, in the export, and in the Site preview, at every page depth.\n175\t  - A draft, unpublished, deleted, or never-existing target renders plain text with no `<a>`.\n176\t  - Publishing the target and re-running the export turns it into a link.\n177\t  - **Reuse:** delete the Report a link points to, create a new Report (which may take the old id), and the link is still plain text and marked \"Item deleted\", never a link to the new Report.\n178\t  - Refs are backfilled for existing rows, unique, and unchanged by editing the title or slug.\n179\t  - A new item's ref never equals a ref in `deleted_refs`. Tested by forcing the generator to return a tombstoned ref first: the insert retries and succeeds with a different one.\n180\t  - An absolute image URL in a body renders no `<img>`.\n181\t  - `http:`, `javascript:`, root-absolute, and relative hand-typed hrefs submitted through the Markdown fallback render as plain text.\n182\t  - The crawler still fails on a root-absolute or non-`https`/`mailto` absolute URL, and a test proves it by injecting one.\n183\t- **Tables:** Excel-style HTML becomes a Markdown table. Numeric-column detection works across the formats listed above.\n184\t- **Charts:**\n185\t  - Grammar: every required key missing, every unknown key, every wrong type, duplicate keys, `NaN`/`Infinity`, over-long strings, newlines in strings, mismatched `values` lengths, too many categories or series, and a block over 32 KB are each rejected, **on both the Editor and the Markdown fallback save paths**. Canonical serialization is stable (saving it again changes nothing).\n186\t  - Parsing is tested for every numeric, missing, suppressed, currency, and unit-conflict case.\n187\t  - **Structural allowlist test:** for a set of charts (every type, 1 and 4 series, negatives, missing and suppressed cells, all optional fields), the rendered figure is parsed with `html.parser`. The test collects every element name and every attribute name and asserts both sets are subsets of the fixed vocabulary. It asserts every `fill`/`stroke` is a palette constant, every `class` is a fixed name, and every `id` matches `chart-<nonce>-<n>-title`, with no `href`, `style`, or `on*` anywhere.\n188\t  - Hostile writer strings (`<script>`, `\"><svg onload=…>`, `javascript:`, `</title>`, `&`) in every text field appear only as escaped text content, which the same parse confirms.\n189\t  - Placeholders: a writer who types the placeholder shape into the body gets it rendered as inert text. Two charts get distinct placeholders.\n190\t  - An invalid block reaching render outputs only the fixed \"could not be shown\" text.\n191\t  - Bar charts have a zero baseline. \"Show the data\" preserves the original notation. The privacy note appears exactly once.\n192\t- **Site preview:** a draft's Site preview shows the banner and uses the public stylesheet. A draft Report appears in its own preview's nav but not in any other page or preview. Nothing is saved. Login and CSRF are required.\n193\t- **Draft leak and export:** T08's crawl test still passes, with no draft content in `site/`, and the export is still identical to the live site.\n194\t- **Browser behaviour** (toolbar, paste, the table controls, the chart dialog, the unsaved-changes warning) is checked by hand in Chrome and Safari. These checks add to the pytest suite and never replace it. Each ticket's closing comment records, for each check:\n195\t  - the browser and exact version\n196\t  - the viewport size\n197\t  - the actions performed, step by step\n198\t  - the observed result, with pass or fail\n199\t  - the screenshots as supporting evidence\n200\t\n201\t## Out of Scope\n202\t\n203\t- Pie, stacked, scatter, and dual-axis charts. Chart colour choice.\n204\t- Autosave, revision history, and collaborative editing.\n205\t- Uploading a pasted or dropped picture (it's refused, with a pointer to \"Insert image\").\n206\t- A Markdown source toggle for writers.\n207\t- Underline, fonts, colours, text alignment, code blocks, horizontal rules.\n208\t- Embeds (Tableau Public, Power BI), which is ADR-004 unchanged.\n209\t- Site preview of list pages (home, Data Bites index). The preview shows only the item's own page.\n210\t- The admin console's visual design pass, which gets its own spec later.\n211\t\n212\t## Tickets\n213\t\n214\t- #15 T12: Site preview\n215\t- #16 T13: Editor (ADR-005)\n216\t- #17 T14: Links to Reports and Data Bites\n217\t- #18 T15: Tables in the Editor\n218\t- #19 T16: Chart rendering (ADR-006)\n219\t- #20 T17: Chart builder\n220\t- #21 T18: Chart images in the Editor\n221\t\n222\t\n223\t-----\n224\t# Kenyon Office of Institutional Research (IR) CMS\n225\t\n226\tA CMS for Kenyon College's Office of Institutional Research: a two-person office\n227\t(Director + Analyst/intern staff) that publishes survey results, data briefs,\n228\tand durable reference documents like the Factbook and Common Data Set.\n229\t\n230\t## Language\n231\t\n232\t**Director**:\n233\tThe admin role. Modeled on the real office's Associate VP for Institutional\n234\tResearch — the only person who can publish or edit a Report, manage user\n235\taccounts, and deactivate access.\n236\t_Avoid_: Admin, superuser\n237\t\n238\t**Analyst**:\n239\tThe editor role. Each intern gets their own named Analyst account (see\n240\tADR-003). Can draft and publish Data Bites directly; can draft but not\n241\tpublish or edit Reports. Any Analyst may edit any other Analyst's draft\n242\t(shift continuity), though the original author is preserved.\n243\t_Avoid_: Editor, intern (interns are Analysts, not a separate role), staff\n244\t\n245\t**Data Bite**:\n246\tA Post: a short, dated item — a survey result, an enrollment snapshot, an\n247\tannouncement. The frequent, low-stakes content type. Analysts can publish\n248\tthese without Director approval.\n249\t_Avoid_: Update, post, announcement, article\n250\t\n251\t**Report**:\n252\tA Page: a durable, cite-able reference document — the Factbook, a Common Data\n253\tSet, the Survey Coordination Policy. Appears in public navigation. Only the\n254\tDirector can publish or edit a Report, even one an Analyst drafted.\n255\t_Avoid_: Page, document\n256\t\n257\t**Draft**:\n258\tContent (a Data Bite or Report) that has been saved but not published. Never\n259\tappears on the public site. Used for unreleased data, e.g. enrollment numbers\n260\tstill being verified before the official count.\n261\t_Avoid_: Unpublished, pending\n262\t\n263\t**Published**:\n264\tContent visible on the public site. The one-way gate: a Report only crosses\n265\tit with Director action.\n266\t_Avoid_: Live, public\n267\t\n268\t**Chart image**:\n269\tAn *uploaded* PNG, JPEG, or WebP picture (usually a chart made in Excel, R,\n270\tor Tableau) that a Data Bite or Report shows inline, placed in its body and\n271\tstored there as `image:<name>`. It belongs to its item and is published with\n272\tit (ADR-004). Not a **Chart**, which the CMS draws from data, and not a\n273\tReport's **attached file**, which is a PDF offered for download.\n274\t_Avoid_: figure, graphic, media, attachment\n275\t\n276\t**Chart**:\n277\tA bar, horizontal bar, or line chart the CMS *draws* from data typed or\n278\tpasted into it, shown inline in a Data Bite or Report body with its data\n279\tavailable as a table (spec #14). Stored in the body as a `chart` block the\n280\twriter never sees. Not a **Chart image**, which is made elsewhere and uploaded.\n281\t_Avoid_: graph, plot, visualization\n282\t\n283\t**Editor**:\n284\tThe visual body editor on a Data Bite's or Report's edit page: a toolbar,\n285\ttables edited in place, Charts, and Chart images, with no Markdown in sight.\n286\tThe body is still stored as Markdown (spec #14).\n287\t_Avoid_: WYSIWYG, rich text, rich-text editor\n288\t\n289\t**Site preview**:\n290\tA Draft (or unsaved edits) rendered as its public page would look, with the\n291\tsite's nav and stylesheet and a \"Draft preview, not published\" banner. Saves\n292\tnothing and publishes nothing.\n293\t_Avoid_: live view\n294\t\n295\t**Confirmation**:\n296\tThe one-line message the admin console shows, once, after a save, publish,\n297\tupload, delete, or user change succeeds (`app/flash.py`). Fixed text only:\n298\tnever a title, email, filename, or password. A refused action gets an error,\n299\tnot a Confirmation.\n300\t_Avoid_: flash, toast, notification, success message\n301\t\n302\t**Factbook**:\n303\tA specific Report: the office's running reference document of admissions,\n304\tenrollment, diversity, and academic program statistics.\n305\t\n306\t**Common Data Set (CDS)**:\n307\tA specific Report: a standardized annual institutional data submission,\n308\tpublished publicly.\n309\t\n310\t**Survey Calendar**:\n311\tA specific Report: the schedule of past, current, and upcoming surveys the\n312\toffice runs (e.g. faculty/staff surveys, external review surveys).\n313\t-----\n314\tdocs:\n315\tadr\n316\tagents\n317\thandoff\n318\tmanual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md\n319\tmp2-grading-rubric_20260922.md\n320\tmp2-setup_context-threshold-hook_20260922.md\n321\tprocess\n322\tscreenshots\n323\ttranscripts\n324\t\n325\tdocs/adr:\n326\tADR-001-local-admin-static-public.md\n327\tADR-002-stack.md\n328\tADR-003-split-publish-rights.md\n329\tADR-004-chart-images.md\n330\t\n331\tdocs/agents:\n332\tdomain.md\n333\tissue-tracker.md\n334\t[project]\n335\tname = \"iphs400-mp2-cms\"\n336\tversion = \"0.1.0\"\n337\tdescription = \"IPHS 400 MP2 — a small web CMS with a local admin console and a static public site\"\n338\trequires-python = \">=3.12\"\n339\tdependencies = [\n340\t    \"fastapi>=0.115\",\n341\t    \"uvicorn[standard]>=0.32\",\n342\t    \"jinja2>=3.1\",\n343\t    \"python-multipart>=0.0.12\",   # form posts\n344\t    \"itsdangerous>=2.2\",          # signed session cookies\n345\t    \"argon2-cffi>=23.1\",          # password hashing (never store plain passwords)\n346\t    \"markdown-it-py>=3.0\",        # Markdown -> HTML\n347\t    \"nh3>=0.2\",                   # HTML sanitizer (strips <script> etc.)\n348\t    \"ghp-import>=2.1\",            # push site/ to the gh-pages branch\n349\t]\n350\t\n351\t[dependency-groups]\n352\tdev = [\"pytest>=8.3\", \"httpx>=0.28\"]\n353\t\n354\t[project.scripts]\n355\tcms = \"app.cli:main\"\n356\t\n357\t[tool.pytest.ini_options]\n358\ttestpaths = [\"tests\"]\n359\t\n360\t[build-system]\n361\trequires = [\"hatchling\"]\n362\tbuild-backend = \"hatchling.build\"\n363\t\n364\t[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]\n365\tpackages = [\"app\"]\n366\t"}]},"uuid":"8ec5e3b4-43b7-4117-a378-a8be78dac776","timestamp":"2026-09-30T20:16:11.691Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/davelleat/.claude/projects/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/92814826-9c7e-4d79-92fd-82d4264d2156/tool-results/bxl31gfft.txt","content":"title:\tSpec: Document-style authoring — Editor, tables, Charts, Site preview\nstate:\tOPEN\nauthor:\tDavelleAT (Davelle Ampofo-Twumasi)\nlabels:\tspec\ncomments:\t0\nassignees:\t\nprojects:\t\nmilestone:\t\nissue-type:\t\nparent:\t\nsub-issues:\t\nsub-issues-completed:\t\nblocked-by:\t\nblocking:\t\nnumber:\t14\n--\n## Problem Statement\n\nThe office's writers are IR staff and interns, not web developers, but every Data Bite and Report body is typed as Markdown in a plain textarea. A table means lining up pipes by hand, a chart means making it in Excel, exporting a PNG, uploading it, and typing `image:<name>`, and a link to the Factbook means pasting a URL that breaks if the site moves. The preview under the textarea uses the admin console's styling, so nobody sees the page as a visitor will until after `cms publish`.\n\nGoal: turn the CMS from a Markdown publishing tool into a document-style authoring environment. Nontechnical staff can write, paste, build tables and charts, and preview the exact public result without ever seeing the underlying content format.\n\n## Solution\n\n- The **Editor**, a hand-built visual editor, replaces the Markdown textarea. It has a toolbar, cleans up pasted text, and turns a range pasted from Excel or Sheets into a table. The body is still **stored as Markdown**, so the sanitizer, `cms publish`, and existing content are unchanged (ADR-005).\n- Tables are built and edited in place.\n- A **Chart** is built from data typed or pasted into the CMS and drawn by the server as inline SVG, with its data available as a table (ADR-006, which reverses ADR-004's deferral). Uploaded **Chart images** stay and get an \"Insert image\" button.\n- Links to other Reports and Data Bites are picked from a list and stored by immutable reference, so they stay correct when slugs or the site's address change.\n- A **Site preview** shows the draft as the public page (site nav, stylesheet, date line) beside the Editor and in a new tab, with a \"Draft preview, not published\" banner.\n\nControls are functional and minimally styled. A visual design pass for the admin console comes later, in its own spec.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As an Analyst, I want to write a Data Bite with toolbar buttons for bold, italic, lists, headings, and quotes, so that I never have to learn Markdown.\n2. As an Analyst, I want to paste text from Word or Google Docs and keep its bold, lists, headings, and links but not its fonts or colours, so that pasted content matches the site.\n3. As an Analyst, I want to paste a range from Excel or Sheets and get a table, so that I don't retype numbers.\n4. As an Analyst, I want to edit a table in place and add or remove rows and columns, so that fixing a number takes one click.\n5. As a visitor, I want numeric table columns right-aligned, so that figures line up and compare easily.\n6. As an Analyst, I want to build a bar or line chart by typing or pasting data, and see it drawn as I go, so that a survey result gets a chart without Excel exports.\n7. As an Analyst, I want a clear message next to a cell the chart can't read, so that I know exactly what to fix.\n8. As an Analyst, I want suppressed values (`*`, `<10`) to be accepted and marked as suppressed, so that a chart respects small-cell privacy rules.\n9. As a visitor using a screen reader, I want each Chart named by its title and its data available as a table, so that I get the numbers without seeing the chart.\n10. As an Analyst, I want to link to another Report or Data Bite by picking it from a list, so that the link survives slug changes and the site moving.\n11. As a visitor, I want a link to an item that isn't published to show as plain text, not a broken link.\n12. As a Director, I want to be told which items link to an item before I delete it, so that I know which pages will lose a link.\n13. As an Analyst, I want to insert an uploaded Chart image with a button that requires a description, so that I can't forget the alt text.\n14. As an Analyst or Director, I want to see the draft exactly as the public page will look, at desktop and phone widths, so that I catch problems before publishing.\n15. As an Analyst or Director, I want a warning before I leave a page with unsaved changes, so that I don't lose work.\n16. As a Director, I want opening and saving an untouched item to leave its stored body byte-for-byte unchanged, so that the Editor never rewrites content nobody edited.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n### Editor and storage (T13, ADR-005)\n\n- **No dependency.** The Editor is `contenteditable` plus a toolbar in vanilla JS with no build step (ADR-002). It supports current Chrome, Safari, and Firefox.\n- **Markdown stays the storage format.** On load, the server renders the body to Editor HTML with the existing pipeline. On save, the Editor posts its HTML, and the server sanitizes it with nh3 and converts it to Markdown with stdlib `html.parser` (a new module, testable with pytest).\n- **Toolbar:** bold, italic, bulleted list, numbered list, link, Section (H2), Subsection (H3), block quote. The title stays the only H1. There's no underline, font, colour, or alignment, because Markdown can't hold them.\n- **Base version:** the edit form carries `item_base`, a SHA-256 hash of the item's stored `title`, `slug`, and `body` as the page loaded them. The form saves all three, so all three are covered. A hash of the body alone would let a stale tab overwrite someone else's newer title or slug. On save, if the stored item's hash no longer matches (someone else saved in between), the whole save is refused with \"This item changed since you opened it. Reload to see the latest version.\" Nothing is merged, and no field is written.\n- **Untouched is byte-for-byte:** the Editor posts `body_dirty=0` until the writer's first change. With `body_dirty=0` and a matching `item_base`, the server keeps the stored body exactly and ignores the posted HTML. The client can only choose \"keep what is stored\", so trusting the flag grants nothing. Opening the Editor never rewrites the body.\n- **An edited body is saved in standard Markdown form:** any body the Editor has changed is rewritten in one standard form.\n- **Locked blocks:** a top-level block the Editor can't represent shows as a read-only block reading \"This part can't be edited here\" (with a Remove button), and its original bytes are kept even when blocks around it are edited. No current content triggers this. The mechanism:\n  - **Detection:** the stored body is parsed with markdown-it. A top-level block is *supported* only if it and everything inside it is in the Editor's set: paragraph, H2, H3, bulleted and numbered list, block quote, table, a valid `chart` fence, and inline bold, italic, line break, links allowed under T14, and `image:<name>` images. Anything else locks the whole top-level block it sits in, e.g. a code block, raw HTML, H1 or H4 and deeper, a horizontal rule, or an inline code span in a paragraph. Its exact source bytes come from the token's line map.\n  - **Before rendering Editor HTML:** each locked block is cut out of the source and replaced by an opaque token (`locked-<n>`, n being its position among the stored body's locked blocks). The remaining Markdown is rendered, and the token becomes the read-only block. The block's **raw Markdown bytes never reach the browser**: not in the Editor's HTML, not in a hidden field, not in an attribute. What the writer sees is that block's **sanitized rendered HTML** from the ordinary pipeline, displayed read-only next to its token.\n  - **On save:** each token in the posted HTML is replaced by the original fragment taken from the **stored database body** (checked by `item_base`), never from anything the client sent. A token that doesn't exist in the stored body, or appears more than once, refuses the save. A missing token means the writer removed that block, which is allowed.\n- **Paste:** only supported formatting survives. An HTML table on the clipboard (from Excel or Sheets) becomes an Editor table. A pasted or dropped picture is refused with a message pointing to \"Insert image\" (T18).\n- **Unsaved changes:** a `beforeunload` warning is shown when the Editor is dirty. There's no autosave, since that would publish half-finished text on a published Data Bite.\n- **Fallback:** the Editor takes over the existing `body` textarea. If the script fails, the textarea still works and posts Markdown as it does today.\n\n### Links (T14)\n\n- **The rule, restated:** every *site-owned* link and asset uses a relative path. Only an *explicit external link* (`<a href>`) may be absolute, and only as `https:` or `mailto:`. The Editor's link dialog refuses anything else (`http:`, `javascript:`, root-absolute `/…`, other schemes) with a message.\n- **The link pipeline enforces it for every body, however it was saved:** at render time, an `<a>` keeps its href only if the href is `https:`, `mailto:`, or a site reference (below) that resolves. Anything else renders as its link text with no `<a>`. This covers the Markdown fallback and any stored content, not only the Editor. Consequence (approved): a relative path typed by hand, e.g. `[CDS](reports/cds.html)`, renders as plain text, because it would break depending on page depth. Site links are made with the picker.\n- **Images follow the same rule:** only `image:<name>` renders an `<img>`. An absolute image URL (e.g. `![Logo](https://…)`) renders nothing (approved). A hot-linked image sits outside the draft gate that ADR-004 exists for. T14 updates `tests/test_t10_chart_images.py`'s \"other image URLs\" test to match.\n- **Stable references, not ids:** SQLite may reuse the highest deleted `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` (noted in `app/data_bites.py` and `app/reports.py`), so the id isn't safe to link by.\n  - Each Data Bite and Report gets an immutable `ref` column: 32 lowercase hex characters from `secrets.token_hex(16)`, set at creation, never edited, never reused. A new ref is checked, in the same transaction as the insert, against **both** tables' live refs and `deleted_refs`. On the (extremely unlikely) collision, a fresh ref is generated and the insert retried, and it fails loudly after 3 attempts.\n  - It's added through `ADDED_COLUMNS`, with existing rows given refs by `init_db`, plus `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` on each table.\n  - A site link is stored as `report:<ref>` or `data-bite:<ref>` and resolved at render time to the page-relative path, like `image:<name>` (ADR-004). Never by title, slug, or id.\n- **Deleted versus never existed:** deleting a Data Bite or Report writes a tombstone row `deleted_refs(kind, ref, deleted_at)` in the same transaction. A ref found in its table is a live or draft item. A ref found only in `deleted_refs` was deleted. A ref in neither never existed (e.g. typed by hand in the fallback).\n- **Unresolvable targets:** a draft, unpublished, deleted, or never-existing target renders as **plain text** (its link text, with no `<a>`), never as an empty or unsafe link. The reference stays stored, so it becomes a link again if its target is published.\n- In the Editor, such links are marked \"Not published: will show as plain text\", \"Item deleted\", or \"Unknown link\".\n- Deleting an item shows the items whose bodies link to it, and the delete isn't blocked.\n- `cms publish` regenerates all of `site/` on every run (`app/publish.py`), so a link becomes live on the first publish after its target is published. No pages need rebuilding individually.\n- **Docs and crawler change together in T14:**\n  - The CLAUDE.md hard rule becomes \"Site-owned links and assets use **relative** paths only. Never `href=\"/...\"` or `src=\"/...\"`. Explicit external links may use `https:` or `mailto:`.\" ADR-001 gets a matching note.\n  - The T07/T08 crawler skips an `<a href>` that is `https:` or `mailto:`. It still fails on any root-absolute path, any other `://` URL, and any `src` that isn't relative, and it still fetches and checks every internal link.\n\n### Tables (T15)\n\n- Edited in place in the Editor, with add/remove row and column controls shown while the cursor is in a table. Stored as a Markdown table (T09 styling and scroll wrapper unchanged).\n- The first row is always the header.\n- **Right-aligned automatically** when every non-empty cell in a column is numeric. Numeric means digits with optional thousands commas, a leading `-` or `$`, a trailing `%`, or accounting parentheses `(3.2)`. Blank, `—`, and `n/a` cells don't stop a column counting as numeric.\n\n### Charts (T16 rendering, ADR-006; T17 builder)\n\n- **Stored** as a fenced block whose info string is exactly `chart`, containing one strict JSON object parsed with stdlib `json`. Writers never see it.\n- **Grammar, version 1:**\n\n  | Key | Required | Type and limits |\n  |---|---|---|\n  | `version` | yes | the integer `1` |\n  | `type` | yes | `\"bar\"`, `\"hbar\"`, or `\"line\"` |\n  | `title` | yes | string, 1 to 120 characters |\n  | `x_label`, `y_label` | no | string, up to 60 characters |\n  | `unit` | no | `{\"text\": string of 1 to 20 characters, \"position\": \"prefix\" or \"suffix\"}` |\n  | `source` | no | string, up to 200 characters |\n  | `categories` | yes | array of 1 to 30 strings for `bar`/`hbar`, or 2 to 60 for `line`; each 1 to 60 characters; no duplicates |\n  | `series` | yes | array of 1 to 4 `{\"name\": string of 1 to 40 characters, \"values\": [...]}`, with names unique and `values` exactly as long as `categories` |\n  | `values[i]` | yes | string, up to 20 characters: the cell **as typed**, parsed at render by the number rules below, so \"as typed\" labels and suppressed notation survive |\n\n  - Every string must be single-line (no control characters, including newlines and tabs) and is Unicode NFC-normalized on save.\n  - Unknown keys, missing required keys, wrong types, duplicate JSON keys (checked with `object_pairs_hook`), `NaN`, `Infinity`, trailing data, and any block over 32 KB make the block **invalid**.\n  - A value cell that fails the number rules is also invalid, unless it's a missing or suppressed value.\n- **Canonical serialization:** keys in the table's order, absent optional keys omitted, `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)`, and a trailing newline inside the fence. The Editor and the fallback both save this form.\n- **Malformed blocks:** validation runs on **every save path**, the Editor and the Markdown fallback alike. A body containing an invalid `chart` block is refused with a form error that names the problem, e.g. \"Chart 2: series 'Fall 2025' has 29 values but 30 categories\". As defense in depth, rendering an invalid block (such as stored content validated under older rules) outputs the fixed text \"This chart could not be shown.\" and nothing else, from no writer-controlled input.\n- **Types:** vertical bar, horizontal bar, line. 1 to 4 series, with a legend when there's more than one. Up to 30 categories for bar charts and 60 for line charts.\n- **Fields:** title (required), x- and y-axis labels (optional), Units (optional; one field in the builder, stored with its prefix or suffix position), Source/note (optional; one line of plain text with no formatting).\n- **Palette:** fixed and accessible, and writers can't choose colours.\n- **Number parsing:** a value may have thousands commas, a leading `-`, accounting parentheses (negative), a trailing `%`, or a leading `$`. Any other currency symbol is an inline error.\n- **Units:** `$` is a unit *prefix* and `%` a unit *suffix*, and the chart stores which one it is. Units typed as a word (\"students\") is a suffix, with a space before it. One chart has one unit, and mixing `$` and `%` is an inline error naming the first conflicting cell. A `%` in the data sets the units to `%` if none are given.\n- **Missing values:** blank, `—`, `n/a`. No bar is drawn, and a line shows a gap.\n- **Suppressed values:** the whole trimmed cell must match `*`, `<N`, `≤N`, or `<=N` (N a whole number).\n  - No mark is drawn.\n  - The data table keeps the original notation.\n  - \"Some values are suppressed for privacy\" appears once under the chart.\n- **Axes:** a bar chart always starts at zero. A line chart may start above zero and says so when it does. Values are labelled as typed, not re-rounded.\n- **Suggested type:** a long category label suggests horizontal bar but doesn't force it.\n- **Accessibility:** the SVG has `role=\"img\"` and the chart title as its accessible name. Under it, a `<details>` \"Show the data\" table is generated from the same data. The public site gets no JavaScript.\n- **Trusted SVG boundary:** nothing inserted after nh3 is sanitized again, so the chart's HTML must be safe because of how it's built, not by filtering.\n  - **Placeholders:** each render generates a fresh `secrets.token_hex(16)` nonce *after* the writer's input is fixed. Each valid chart fence renders as the placeholder `chart-<nonce>-<n>`. After nh3, each placeholder must occur exactly once and is replaced exactly once. A missing, extra, or leftover placeholder fails the render loudly (an exception, and a 500 in the admin console) rather than emitting anything partial.\n  - **Validate first:** a chart is drawn only from a block that passed the full grammar above. Values are parsed to Python `float`s and checked with `math.isfinite`, and anything non-finite is rejected before drawing.\n  - **Fixed vocabulary:** the renderer emits only these elements: `figure`, `figcaption`, `svg`, `g`, `title`, `rect`, `line`, `polyline`, `circle`, `text`, `p`, `small`, `details`, `summary`, `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tr`, `th`, `td`. It emits only these attributes: `class`, `viewBox`, `role`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-hidden`, `id`, `x`, `y`, `x1`, `y1`, `x2`, `y2`, `width`, `height`, `cx`, `cy`, `r`, `points`, `fill`, `stroke`, `stroke-width`, `text-anchor`, `scope`.\n  - **Attribute values:**\n    - Numbers are formatted by the renderer.\n    - `fill` and `stroke` come only from the fixed palette constants.\n    - `class` comes only from fixed class names.\n    - `id` is only `chart-<nonce>-<n>-title`.\n    - There's never an `href`, `style`, `on*`, or URL-bearing attribute.\n  - **Writer text:** every writer-controlled string (title, labels, unit, source, category and series names, cell text) appears only as escaped *text content* (`html.escape`), in both the SVG and the data table. Never as an attribute value, element name, id, class, URL, or CSS.\n  - No uploaded SVG is ever served (ADR-004 unchanged).\n- **Builder (T17):** a dialog with a grid (categories down, series across) that accepts typing and an Excel or Sheets paste. It draws the chart live using the same server rendering, shows errors next to the cells, and has the Units field. In the body, a Chart is a card showing the drawn chart, with Edit and Remove.\n\n### Chart images in the Editor (T18)\n\n- \"Insert image\" lists the item's uploaded Chart images, and a description (alt) is required before inserting. It's stored as `![Description](image:<name>)` as today, and the existing upload, validation, and permissions (ADR-004) are unchanged.\n\n### Site preview (T12)\n\n- The draft is rendered through the public templates, `public_site.CSS`, and the site nav, with the item shown **as if published**: a draft Report appears in the nav. Other drafts stay hidden.\n- It's an embedded frame beside the Editor that drops below it on narrow screens, and it updates as the writer types (debounced, as today).\n- A Desktop/Phone width toggle.\n- \"Preview on site\" opens the same rendering in a new tab, showing the current **unsaved** edits (the form is posted to the tab, and nothing is saved).\n- A \"Draft preview, not published\" banner on every Site preview.\n- Preview routes require login and CSRF, save nothing, and follow the item's permissions (ADR-003).\n\n### Vocabulary\n\n- CONTEXT.md gains **Chart**, **Site preview**, and **Editor**, and **Chart image** is clarified as uploaded.\n- Avoid: graph, WYSIWYG, rich text, live view.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- Behaviour is tested through `TestClient` with the `client` / `client_as(role)` fixtures, as in #1 and #11. The pure modules (HTML → Markdown conversion, chart parsing, SVG drawing) also get direct pytest tests.\n- **Round trip:**\n  - An untouched body posted back is stored byte-for-byte.\n  - A no-change round trip through the standard form renders equivalent HTML, for every seed body and every T09/T10 test fixture.\n  - An edit to one block changes only that block's rendered HTML.\n  - A locked block's bytes survive edits to the blocks around it.\n  - The Editor HTML for a body with locked blocks contains their tokens and their sanitized rendered HTML, and none of their raw Markdown bytes anywhere in the response.\n  - A save with an unknown locked token, a duplicated token, or a forged token that carries its own content is refused. A save with a token removed drops only that block.\n  - A save against a stale `item_base` is refused and changes nothing. **Title/slug conflict:** tab A opens an item, tab B changes only its title (or only its slug) and saves, then tab A saves an untouched body. Tab A's save is refused, and tab B's title and slug survive. A save with `body_dirty=0` stores the old body even when the posted HTML differs.\n- **Sanitizing:** Editor HTML carrying `<script>`, `onerror=`, `style=`, `javascript:` hrefs, root-absolute hrefs, and unknown tags is stored as safe Markdown, with none of it surviving to any render.\n- **Links:**\n  - A `report:<ref>` or `data-bite:<ref>` link renders a correct relative href on the public page, in the export, and in the Site preview, at every page depth.\n  - A draft, unpublished, deleted, or never-existing target renders plain text with no `<a>`.\n  - Publishing the target and re-running the export turns it into a link.\n  - **Reuse:** delete the Report a link points to, create a new Report (which may take the old id), and the link is still plain text and marked \"Item deleted\", never a link to the new Report.\n  - Refs are backfilled for existing rows, unique, and unchanged by editing the title or slug.\n  - A new item's ref never equals a ref in `deleted_refs`. Tested by forcing the generator to return a tombstoned ref first: the insert retries and succeeds with a different one.\n  - An absolute image URL in a body renders no `<img>`.\n  - `http:`, `javascript:`, root-absolute, and relative hand-typed hrefs submitted through the Markdown fallback render as plain text.\n  - The crawler still fails on a root-absolute or non-`https`/`mailto` absolute URL, and a test proves it by injecting one.\n- **Tables:** Excel-style HTML becomes a Markdown table. Numeric-column detection works across the formats listed above.\n- **Charts:**\n  - Grammar: every required key missing, every unknown key, every wrong type, duplicate keys, `NaN`/`Infinity`, over-long strings, newlines in strings, mismatched `values` lengths, too many categories or series, and a block over 32 KB are each rejected, **on both the Editor and the Markdown fallback save paths**. Canonical serialization is stable (saving it again changes nothing).\n  - Parsing is tested for every numeric, missing, suppressed, currency, and unit-conflict case.\n  - **Structural allowlist test:** for a set of charts (every type, 1 and 4 series, negatives, missing and suppressed cells, all optional fields), the rendered figure is parsed with `html.parser`. The test collects every element name and every attribute name and asserts both sets are subsets of the fixed vocabulary. It asserts every `fill`/`stroke` is a palette constant, every `class` is a fixed name, and every `id` matches `chart-<nonce>-<n>-title`, with no `href`, `style`, or `on*` anywhere.\n  - Hostile writer strings (`<script>`, `\"><svg onload=…>`, `javascript:`, `</title>`, `&`) in every text field appear only as escaped text content, which the same parse confirms.\n  - Placeholders: a writer who types the placeholder shape into the body gets it rendered as inert text. Two charts get distinct placeholders.\n  - An invalid block reaching render outputs only the fixed \"could not be shown\" text.\n  - Bar charts have a zero baseline. \"Show the data\" preserves the original notation. The privacy note appears exactly once.\n- **Site preview:** a draft's Site preview shows the banner and uses the public stylesheet. A draft Report appears in its own preview's nav but not in any other page or preview. Nothing is saved. Login and CSRF are required.\n- **Draft leak and export:** T08's crawl test still passes, with no draft content in `site/`, and the export is still identical to the live site.\n- **Browser behaviour** (toolbar, paste, the table controls, the chart dialog, the unsaved-changes warning) is checked by hand in Chrome and Safari. These checks add to the pytest suite and never replace it. Each ticket's closing comment records, for each check:\n  - the browser and exact version\n  - the viewport size\n  - the actions performed, step by step\n  - the observed result, with pass or fail\n  - the screenshots as supporting evidence\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Pie, stacked, scatter, and dual-axis charts. Chart colour choice.\n- Autosave, revision history, and collaborative editing.\n- Uploading a pasted or dropped picture (it's refused, with a pointer to \"Insert image\").\n- A Markdown source toggle for writers.\n- Underline, fonts, colours, text alignment, code blocks, horizontal rules.\n- Embeds (Tableau Public, Power BI), which is ADR-004 unchanged.\n- Site preview of list pages (home, Data Bites index). The preview shows only the item's own page.\n- The admin console's visual design pass, which gets its own spec later.\n\n## Tickets\n\n- #15 T12: Site preview\n- #16 T13: Editor (ADR-005)\n- #17 T14: Links to Reports and Data Bites\n- #18 T15: Tables in the Editor\n- #19 T16: Chart rendering (ADR-006)\n- #20 T17: Chart builder\n- #21 T18: Chart images in the Editor\n\n\n-----\n# Kenyon Office of Institutional Research (IR) CMS\n\nA CMS for Kenyon College's Office of Institutional Research: a two-person office\n(Director + Analyst/intern staff) that publishes survey results, data briefs,\nand durable reference documents like the Factbook and Common Data Set.\n\n## Language\n\n**Director**:\nThe admin role. Modeled on the real office's Associate VP for Institutional\nResearch — the only person who can publish or edit a Report, manage user\naccounts, and deactivate access.\n_Avoid_: Admin, superuser\n\n**Analyst**:\nThe editor role. Each intern gets their own named Analyst account (see\nADR-003). Can draft and publish Data Bites directly; can draft but not\npublish or edit Reports. Any Analyst may edit any other Analyst's draft\n(shift continuity), though the original author is preserved.\n_Avoid_: Editor, intern (interns are Analysts, not a separate role), staff\n\n**Data Bite**:\nA Post: a short, dated item — a survey result, an enrollment snapshot, an\nannouncement. The frequent, low-stakes content type. Analysts can publish\nthese without Director approval.\n_Avoid_: Update, post, announcement, article\n\n**Report**:\nA Page: a durable, cite-able reference document — the Factbook, a Common Data\nSet, the Survey Coordination Policy. Appears in public navigation. Only the\nDirector can publish or edit a Report, even one an Analyst drafted.\n_Avoid_: Page, document\n\n**Draft**:\nContent (a Data Bite or Report) that has been saved but not published. Never\nappears on the public site. Used for unreleased data, e.g. enrollment numbers\nstill being verified before the official count.\n_Avoid_: Unpublished, pending\n\n**Published**:\nContent visible on the public site. The one-way gate: a Report only crosses\nit with Director action.\n_Avoid_: Live, public\n\n**Chart image**:\nAn *uploaded* PNG, JPEG, or WebP picture (usually a chart made in Excel, R,\nor Tableau) that a Data Bite or Report shows inline, placed in its body and\nstored there as `image:<name>`. It belongs to its item and is published with\nit (ADR-004). Not a **Chart**, which the CMS draws from data, and not a\nReport's **attached file**, which is a PDF offered for download.\n_Avoid_: figure, graphic, media, attachment\n\n**Chart**:\nA bar, horizontal bar, or line chart the CMS *draws* from data typed or\npasted into it, shown inline in a Data Bite or Report body with its data\navailable as a table (spec #14). Stored in the body as a `chart` block the\nwriter never sees. Not a **Chart image**, which is made elsewhere and uploaded.\n_Avoid_: graph, plot, visualization\n\n**Editor**:\nThe visual body editor on a Data Bite's or Report's edit page: a toolbar,\ntables edited in place, Charts, and Chart images, with no Markdown in sight.\nThe body is still stored as Markdown (spec #14).\n_Avoid_: WYSIWYG, rich text, rich-text editor\n\n**Site preview**:\nA Draft (or unsaved edits) rendered as its public page would look, with the\nsite's nav and stylesheet and a \"Draft preview, not published\" banner. Saves\nnothing and publishes nothing.\n_Avoid_: live view\n\n**Confirmation**:\nThe one-line message the admin console shows, once, after a save, publish,\nupload, delete, or user change succeeds (`app/flash.py`). Fixed text only:\nnever a title, email, filename, or password. A refused action gets an error,\nnot a Confirmation.\n_Avoid_: flash, toast, notification, success message\n\n**Factbook**:\nA specific Report: the office's running reference document of admissions,\nenrollment, diversity, and academic program statistics.\n\n**Common Data Set (CDS)**:\nA specific Report: a standardized annual institutional data submission,\npublished publicly.\n\n**Survey Calendar**:\nA specific Report: the schedule of past, current, and upcoming surveys the\noffice runs (e.g. faculty/staff surveys, external review surveys).\n-----\ndocs:\nadr\nagents\nhandoff\nmanual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md\nmp2-grading-rubric_20260922.md\nmp2-setup_context-threshold-hook_20260922.md\nprocess\nscreenshots\ntranscripts\n\ndocs/adr:\nADR-001-local-admin-static-public.md\nADR-002-stack.md\nADR-003-split-publish-rights.md\nADR-004-chart-images.md\n\ndocs/agents:\ndomain.md\nissue-tracker.md\n[project]\nname = \"iphs400-mp2-cms\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\ndescription = \"IPHS 400 MP2 — a small web CMS with a local admin console and a static public site\"\nrequires-python = \">=3.12\"\ndependencies = [\n    \"fastapi>=0.115\",\n    \"uvicorn[standard]>=0.32\",\n    \"jinja2>=3.1\",\n    \"python-multipart>=0.0.12\",   # form posts\n    \"itsdangerous>=2.2\",          # signed session cookies\n    \"argon2-cffi>=23.1\",          # password hashing (never store plain passwords)\n    \"markdown-it-py>=3.0\",        # Markdown -> HTML\n    \"nh3>=0.2\",                   # HTML sanitizer (strips <script> etc.)\n    \"ghp-import>=2.1\",            # push site/ to the gh-pages branch\n]\n\n[dependency-groups]\ndev = [\"pytest>=8.3\", \"httpx>=0.28\"]\n\n[project.scripts]\ncms = \"app.cli:main\"\n\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\ntestpaths = [\"tests\"]\n\n[build-system]\nrequires = [\"hatchling\"]\nbuild-backend = \"hatchling.build\"\n\n[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]\npackages = [\"app\"]\n","numLines":366,"startLine":1,"totalLines":366}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"6743f9f6-9755-466e-9a96-86e2ab4f4481","session_id":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"92814826-9c7e-4d79-92fd-82d4264d2156","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}

tests/test_t11_report_chart_images.py\n     473 tests/test_t10_chart_images.py\n    5212 total\n# Domain Docs\n\nHow the engineering skills should consume this repo's domain documentation when exploring the codebase.\n\n## Before exploring, read these\n\n- **`CONTEXT.md`** at the repo root, or\n- **`CONTEXT-MAP.md`** at the repo root if it exists: it points at one `CONTEXT.md` per context. Read each one relevant to the topic.\n- **`docs/adr/`**: read ADRs that touch the area you're about to work in. In multi-context repos, also check `src/<context>/docs/adr/` for context-scoped decisions.\n\nIf any of these files don't exist, **proceed silently**. Don't flag their absence; don't suggest creating them upfront. The `/domain-modeling` skill (reached via `/grill-with-docs` and `/improve-codebase-architecture`) creates them lazily when terms or decisions actually get resolved.\n\n## File structure\n\nSingle-context repo (most repos):\n\n```\n/\n├── CONTEXT.md\n├── docs/adr/\n│   ├── 0001-event-sourced-orders.md\n│   └── 0002-postgres-for-write-model.md\n└── src/\n```\n\nMulti-context repo (presence of `CONTEXT-MAP.md` at the root):\n\n```\n/\n├── CONTEXT-MAP.md\n├── docs/adr/                          ← system-wide decisions\n└── src/\n    ├── ordering/\n    │   ├── CONTEXT.md\n    │   └── docs/adr/                  ← context-specific decisions\n    └── billing/\n        ├── CONTEXT.md\n        └── docs/adr/\n```\n\n## Use the glossary's vocabulary\n\nWhen your output names a domain concept (in an issue title, a refactor proposal, a hypothesis, a test name), use the term as defined in `CONTEXT.md`. Don't drift to synonyms the glossary explicitly avoids.\n\nIf the concept you need isn't in the glossary yet, that's a signal: either you're inventing language the project doesn't use (reconsider) or there's a real gap (note it for `/domain-modeling`).\n\n## Flag ADR conflicts\n\nIf your output contradicts an existing ADR, surface it explicitly rather than silently overriding:\n\n> _Contradicts ADR-0007 (event-sourced orders), but worth reopening because…_\n# Issue tracker: GitHub\n\nIssues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.\n\n## Conventions\n\n- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.\n\n- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.\n- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.\n- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.\n- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.\n- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.\n- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body \"<answer>\"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.\n# Data Bites and Reports carry chart images, referenced from the Markdown body\n\n**Status:** accepted (reverses the original spec's \"uploads for Data Bites\" exclusion, #1; spec #11)\n\nThe office's content is mostly numbers, and it already makes charts of them\nin Excel, R, and Tableau. The original spec kept Data Bites Markdown-only and\ngave Reports one attached PDF, so a chart had nowhere to go except an image\nlink to some other host. That puts it outside the draft/publish gate, and it\nbreaks when the other host changes.\n\nWe decided: **both** Data Bites and Reports can carry chart images, uploaded on\nthe item's edit page and placed in its Markdown body as `image:<name>`.\nData Bites were included on purpose, not only Reports. A Data Bite such as\n\"Fall enrollment snapshot\" is exactly where a chart is wanted.\n\n**Uploaded files, not generated charts.** The CMS stores and shows a chart\nsomeone made elsewhere; it does not draw one from data. That keeps the stack\nunchanged (no charting or image library, `pyproject.toml` is fixed), works\nwith whatever tool the office already uses, and leaves no JavaScript on the\npublic site. Charts drawn from a data block in the Markdown were considered\nand deferred as a possible stretch. Embeds (Tableau Public, Power BI) were\nrejected, because they need `<iframe>` through the sanitizer.\n\n**Raster only: PNG, JPEG, WebP. No SVG.** An SVG is a document that can carry\n`<script>` and event handlers, and serving an uploaded one from the site's own\norigin would reopen the hole the Markdown sanitizer closes. Content is checked\nby signature, the way T05 checks a PDF, because there is no decoding library.\n\n**`image:<name>`, resolved at render time.** The body never holds a path. The\nMarkdown pipeline turns `image:<name>` into the URL for the page being rendered\n(admin preview, public page, or export), so one stored body works at every\ndepth and the published HTML stays relative. An unknown name renders nothing.\n\n**An image belongs to its item.** It is public only while that item is\npublished, and it follows that item's permissions (ADR-003 unchanged): any\nAnalyst may manage a Data Bite's images or a draft Report's, and only the\nDirector a published Report's. Deleting the item deletes its images.\n\nOne consequence, accepted: an image is public for as long as its item is\npublished, whether or not the body places it. An image uploaded to a\npublished Data Bite is served, and exported by `cms publish`, at once, even\nbefore the body references it. A chart that isn't ready to be seen goes on a\ndraft, not on a published
