{"parentUuid":"a27c2529-3573-4f4e-b189-90f775808b48","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"28247e96-0075-4c3d-95c3-a03b076f199b","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/davelleat/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Review changes since 03ad7fd (T13, issue #16; spec #14)"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"0ac15e82-e86b-4221-9e91-2129878227f2","timestamp":"2026-09-30T20:56:46.748Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01VNSwRq9T3bYWRgqegj2KbE","session_id":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"92814826-9c7e-4d79-92fd-82d4264d2156","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}

Each is then passed to `posted(...)`. A single FastAPI dependency returning `editor.Posted` would bundle it. `form_after(posted, title, slug, base, stored, image_name)` at `app/editor.py:299` takes six positional parameters, and `title`/`slug`/`body` travel together.\n  - **Middle Man:** `app/routes/editing.py:posted()` only calls `editor.Posted(...)` with a `== \"1\"` coercion. The module docstring frames all of it as \"the Editor's server side\", so this is borderline and acceptable for now.\n  - **Repeated work:** `tokenize(stored).locked` runs again in `restore` (`:170`), `editor_html` (`:202`) and `Posted.untouched` for each request. The report follows:\n  **Spec review: T13 (`git diff 03ad7fd...HEAD`)**\n  \n  I checked the diff against #16, the \"Editor and storage\" section of #14, the T13 testing bullets, CONTEXT.md and the five decisions made in the session. The full suite passes (541 tests), and no existing test file changed. The seed bodies now tokenize with 0 locked blocks.\n  \n  **(a) Missing or partial requirements**\n  None of substance. Every acceptance criterion has code and a test behind it:\n  - toolbar\n  - paste cleanup, table kept\n  - picture refused\n  - `item_base` and `body_dirty`\n  - untouched body kept byte-for-byte\n  - standard form\n  - locked-block tokenizing, restoring and refusing\n  - leave warning\n  - fallback\n  - ADR-005 and the CONTEXT.md link\n  - all five listed test groups, including the title/slug conflict\n  \n  **(b) Behaviour nobody asked for (all small)**\n  - **Leave warning fires on other fields too.** `static/editor.js:103-107` sets `unsaved` when the title, slug or file field changes. The spec says the warning shows \"when the Editor is dirty\". This is broader, but harmless.\n  - **Keyboard shortcuts.** `static/editor.js:140-149` adds Ctrl/Cmd+K for a link and blocks Ctrl/Cmd+U. Nobody asked for these.\n  - **Missing-base refusal.** `app/editor.py:329` refuses an Editor post that carries no base, with the `NEEDS_BASE` message. It's extra hardening beyond the spec.\n  \n  **(c) Implemented, but may be wrong**\n  1. **A post with no `item_base` skips the stale check.** \"The form carries `item_base` … A stale `item_base` refuses the whole save.\" `app/editor.py:327` only checks when `base` is non-empty, and the routes pass `base=item_base or None` (`app/routes/data_bites.py:327`, `app/routes/reports.py:498`). The template always sends `item_base` on edit pages (`templates/admin/_content_fields.html:2-4`), so a real browser is covered, including the fallback. A hand-made post without a base still overwrites, though. The likely reason is to keep the older tests passing unchanged. That's defensible, but it's a gap between the spec and the code, so it should be noted in the closing comment.\n  2. **After a stale refusal with an edited body, locked blocks can show the wrong content.** Decision 3 says a stale save \"keeps the writer's unsaved title/slug/body on screen\". `form_after` returns tokens numbered against the old stored body (`app/editor.py:307`). `_edit_page` then renders them against the current body, `now[\"body\"]` (`app/routes/data_bites.py:301`, `app/routes/reports.py:472`). If tab B added or removed a locked block, tab A may see the wrong block or an empty one. Only the display is affected, because the save stays refused until reload.\n  3. **A refused forged post re-opens with an empty body.** When `posted.markdown` raises (a forged or moved token), `form_after` falls back to `posted.body` (`app/editor.py:308-309`). With the script running, the textarea is disabled, so that value is empty and the Editor re-opens blank. Only a hand-crafted post can trigger this, so it's low severity.\n  4. **Stored reference-style links break in a locked block.** A definition like `[x]: https://…` is not a block, so an Editor save drops it. A locked block that used that definition keeps its bytes but loses the link. The spec only promises \"original bytes are kept\", so this passes on the letter, but the rendered block changes. ADR-005 records it under Consequences.\n</agent-message>"}

The Safari check was\n    waived by the project owner.\n    \n    Closes #15\n    \n    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n## /code-review of T12 (52015b8), and how each finding was resolved\n\nCommits: `52015b8` T12: Site preview · `9fd3e9e` review fixes. Suite: 337 passed (31 new in `tests/test_t12_site_preview.py`; T07/T08 crawl and draft-leak tests pass).\n\n### Standards (no hard violations)\n\n| Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|\n| `preview_site_file` serves admin-only draft files but lives in `app/routes/public.py` (\"published content only\") | **Fixed.** It's now in `app/routes/site_preview.py`, and `routes/public.py` is published-only again |\n| The PDF `FileResponse` is duplicated, and the response type was picked by `stored.suffix == \".pdf\"` | **Fixed.** `public.pdf_response` is shared, and `site_file` is given the chart images and the Report's file separately (`report_image_files`, `report_pdf_file`) |\n| `Page._render(self, **preview)` is a kwargs bag for one value | **Fixed.** It's now `preview_base: str \\| None` |\n| The new create-form preview routes had no docstrings; `_stored_images(module, …)` had no type | **Fixed.** Docstrings added; `module: ModuleType` |\n| The preview nav's sort key copies `reports.list_published`'s order | **Fixed.** A comment now names that order |\n| `_site_preview` and the route pairs are duplicated across `routes/data_bites.py` and `routes/reports.py` | **Kept.** Parallel per-type route modules are the repo's pattern (the old `_image_src` was duplicated the same way) |\n| `body:has(.admin-site-preview)` is broad, and admin rules ship in `style.css` | **Kept.** Scoped by an `admin-` class, following the `.admin-confirmation` precedent. The admin visual pass (out of scope, spec #14) can move admin CSS out |\n\n### Spec\n\n| Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|\n| A draft Report's own nav link in its preview went to the public page, which 404s | **Fixed.** It opens that Report's Site preview as saved (tested) |\n| Other links in the preview (home, other Reports, list pages) go to the published pages, without the banner | **By design.** List pages are out of scope (\"The preview shows only the item's own page\"), and links never reach a draft |\n| An unsaved **slug** isn't reflected | **Deliberate.** The slug changes only hrefs, which no reader sees. The preview keeps the saved slug so it finds the item's files at the paths it gives them (`public_site._as_if_published`). Title and body are live |\n| \"Preview on site\" on a Report posts the whole multipart form, a chosen PDF included, which is discarded unread | **Accepted.** Nothing is saved (tested); avoiding it needs JS on a no-JS path |\n| \"Relative links at every depth\": previewed pages all sit at depth 1 | Tested at that depth. Links go up to the root (`../style.css`) and down to depth 3 (`../images/<type>/<slug>/<name>`), and each one is fetched |\n| Safari browser check not done | **Open.** See below |\n\n### Browser check\n\n**Chrome 154.0.0.0** (macOS), local server with seeded demo content, signed in as the demo Analyst.\n\n| Viewport | Action | Observed |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1280 | Open the draft Report \"Common Data Set 2026-27\" | The frame sits beside the fields, with the banner and the public stylesheet (banner rule computed: 4px border). The nav lists the draft CDS and Survey Calendar, and the other draft is hidden. `docs/screenshots/site-preview-report-draft-1280.jpg` |\n| 1280 | Type `## Unsaved heading` and a table in the body | The frame re-renders with an `<h2>` and a table, with no status message. `<base>` = `/admin/reports/2/preview/reports/common-data-set-2026-27.html`. `site-preview-typing-1280.jpg` |\n| 1280 | Click \"Preview on site\" | A new tab opens at `/admin/reports/2/preview` with the same unsaved rendering and the banner. `site-preview-new-tab-1280.jpg` |\n| 1280 | Click Phone | The frame is 390px wide, and `aria-pressed` moves from Desktop to Phone |\n| 1280 | Log out in the background, then type | \"Preview is not updating. Reload the page (you may need to log in again).\" |\n| — | Check the database | The report rows are unchanged (body, `updated_at`) |\n| 390 | Open the Data Bites create page | The frame is below the fields, with the banner and an empty body. The page scrolls sideways because of the list **table** above, which predates T12 and isn't touched here. `site-preview-create-390.jpg` |\n| 390 | Edit the draft Data Bite | The frame is below \"Save changes\", with no sideways scroll (scrollWidth = innerWidth = 386). `site-preview-edit-390.jpg` |\n\nScreenshots are in the repo under `docs/screenshots/`.\n\n**Safari:** not yet checked. It will be recorded here before this issue closes.\n\n**Safari:** the check was waived by the project owner. The browser check stands on Chrome 154 at 390 and 1280 (see the comment above). {"parentUuid":"0ab3ea1d-1176-46d6-a1e1-32cb71af3732","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfaJVDqg3T3Seu5b27GbL","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01MsAb1FMzHyvjmyEg6KQFNd","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/92814826-9c7e-4d79-92fd-82d4264d2156/scratchpad/t13-review-comment.md","content":"## /code-review of T13 (03ad7fd...69661aa), and how each finding was resolved\n\nCommits:\n- `26b2db6` Editor server side\n- `1045693` routes\n- `8292342` the Editor's script\n- `0928da7` ADR-005\n- `69661aa` review fixes\n\nThe suite passes: 541 tests, 204 of them new in `tests/test_t13_*.py`. No test file from before T13 was changed.\n\nDecisions made in the session:\n- The fallback textarea holds `locked-<n>` lines in place of locked blocks.\n- The seed demo note no longer has a code span.\n- A stale save keeps the writer's edits on screen with the old `item_base`.\n\n### Standards (no hard violations)\n\n| Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|\n| `app/editor.py` imports `hashlib` and `json` but doesn't use them (`item_base` moved to `app/content.py`) | **Fixed.** Removed |\n| ADR-005 says \"rich-text editor library\", a word the glossary says to avoid | **Fixed.** Now \"visual editor library\" |\n| `_LINK_SCHEMES` is defined in both `app/editor.py` and `app/markdown_form.py` | **Fixed.** `markdown_form.LINK_SCHEMES` is the one definition |\n| The token-paragraph check is repeated twice in `app/editor.py` | **Fixed.** `_token_number(block)` |\n| `body` / `body_html` / `body_dirty` travel together across six route signatures (Data Clump), and `posted()` only delegates (Middle Man) | **Fixed.** `editing.posted` is now a route dependency that returns `editor.Posted` |\n| `_images()` and the refused-save status are duplicated across `routes/data_bites.py` and `routes/reports.py` | **Fixed.** `editing.image_links` and `editing.refused_status`. Each route module keeps a one-line `_images` that names its own id parameter |\n| Unclear names: `now`, `_normalized`, and `sent` next to `posted` | **Fixed.** `current`, `_with_lf`, and `posted` throughout |\n| Three blank lines in places | **Fixed** |\n| `form_after` takes six parameters | **Kept.** Each is a distinct input (the post, title, slug, base, stored body, image mapping) |\n| `app/editor.py` covers tokenizing, rendering, save rules and form dicts (Divergent Change), and one request parses the stored body several times | **Kept.** They are all \"the Editor's server side\" (module docstring). The re-parsing is a few milliseconds per page |\n\n### Spec\n\n| Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|\n| A post with no `item_base` skips the stale check, so a hand-made post can still overwrite | **Kept, recorded here.** Every edit page, the fallback included, always sends `item_base`. Editor HTML posted without one is refused. A post with neither is how every test before T13 saves, and \"All existing tests pass unchanged\" |\n| After a stale refusal with an edited body, the writer's tokens are shown against the current body, so a locked block can show the wrong content if the other tab changed the locked blocks | **Kept.** Only the display is affected: the save stays refused until a reload, which shows the current version |\n| A refused post whose locked block was filled in reopened with an empty Editor | **Fixed.** It reopens on the stored body (tested) |\n| A link reference definition (`[x]: https://…`) is dropped when the Editor rewrites a body, so a locked block that uses it loses its link | **Recorded** in ADR-005 under Consequences. No seed or fixture body has one |\n| Beyond the ticket: the leave warning also covers title, slug and file changes, and there are Ctrl/Cmd+K (link) and Ctrl/Cmd+U (blocked: Markdown has no underline) shortcuts | **Kept.** They serve \"a warning when leaving with unsaved changes\" and \"no underline\" |\n\n### Browser check\n\n**Chrome 154.0.8037.58** (macOS). Local server on a scratch database seeded with `scripts/seed_demo.py`, plus a draft \"Survey response rates\" with two locked blocks (a code fence and a paragraph with an inline code span). Signed in as the demo Analyst.\n\n| Viewport | Actions | Observed | Result |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1272 | Open the draft with locked blocks | The toolbar and the editable body appear. Both locked blocks are read-only, show \"This part can't be edited here.\" with a Remove button, and show rendered HTML (the code as `<pre>`). The Site preview is beside them. `docs/screenshots/body-editor-locked-blocks-1272.jpg` | Pass |\n| 1272 | Type \" Spring 2026\" at the end of the first paragraph, then click Section | It becomes an `<h2>`, and the Site preview follows (H2, with the locked code block restored by the server) | Pass |\n| 1272 | Save changes | The stored body is `## Response rates by class year. Spring 2026`, the fence and code-span paragraph byte for byte, `- First-year: **62%**`, `> Rates…` | Pass |\n| 1272 | Create page. Paste (synthetic `ClipboardEvent`) Google Docs HTML: H1, Arial red text, `font-weight:700`/`font-style:italic` spans, an `https:` link, a `javascript:` link, a list of `<li><p>` | `<h2>`. Plain, **bold**, *italic*. The `https:` link is kept and the `javascript:` one is text only. The list items have no `<p>`. No style, font or colour survives | Pass |\n| 1272 | Paste Word HTML: `MsoNormal` bold, and an `MsoListParagraph` run with `mso-list:Ignore` markers \"1.\" and \"2.\", plus an `<img>` | Bold is kept, the paragraphs become an `<ol>` without the markers, and the picture is left out with a message | Pass |\n| 1272 | Paste an Excel table (`col`, `xl65` classes, `mso-number-format`) | A basic `<table>` with no attributes | Pass |\n| 1272 | Paste only a PNG file, then drop a PNG file | Both are refused (default prevented, no `<img>`), with \"Pictures can't be pasted or dropped into the body. Upload the picture under \"Chart images\" instead.\" (\"Insert image\" comes with T18) | Pass |\n| 1272 | Select a word, click Link, enter `http://www.kenyon.edu`, press Enter | \"Links must start with https:// or mailto:.\" The form is not submitted | Pass |\n| 1272 | Enter `https://www.kenyon.edu/ir` and press Enter | `<a href=\"https://www.kenyon.edu/ir\">` is added and the panel closes. Save draft stores `[Fresh](https://www.kenyon.edu/ir).` | Pass |\n| 1272 | With unsaved edits, fire `beforeunload`; then fire it on a freshly opened page | Cancelled (the warning shows) with edits, not on the fresh page. Synthetic event: a real dialog blocks the automation | Pass |\n| 1272 | Open the published \"Fall enrollment snapshot\" (table) and save with no change | The stored body's bytes are identical before and after (only `updated_at` moves) | Pass |\n| 390 and 768 | The draft with locked blocks, in same-origin frames of exactly those widths (the window couldn't be resized) | 768: no sideways scroll. 390: the locked code line first overflowed (scrollWidth 552). Fixed with `.admin-editor-locked pre { overflow-x: auto; }`; now scrollWidth 375 and the code scrolls in its own box. `body-editor-390-and-768.jpg` | Pass (after fix) |\n| 700 | The edit page's own HTML with the `editor.js` tag removed (script fails to load) | The required textarea is shown, holding Markdown with `locked-0` / `locked-1` lines and no locked source. `body-editor-no-script-fallback.jpg` | Pass |\n\n**Still to check by hand:**\n- **Safari:** not yet checked.\n- **Real paste:** a copy from Word and from Google Docs through the real clipboard (the pastes above used synthetic clipboard data).\n- **Leave dialog:** the browser's own dialog.\n- **No JavaScript:** the fallback with JavaScript turned off in browser settings.\n\nThese will be recorded here before this issue You should see no colours or fonts, formatting kept, and a message about the picture. Paste a small Excel or Sheets range and you should get a table.\n3. **Leave warning (both browsers):** type in the body, then click \"All Data Bites\". The browser should ask before leaving. On a page you haven't touched, it shouldn't ask.\n4. **No JavaScript:** turn JavaScript off (Chrome: Settings → Privacy and security → Site settings → JavaScript; Safari: Settings → Security). Open `/admin/data-bites/3`. You should see the plain Markdown textarea with `locked-0` and `locked-1` lines.
